metadata.cross_year_anchor_note: 多年份扩样任务：本标注与 AMD FY2023 确认版（D1=3/D2=2/D3=3/D4=1/D5=3→2.40）显式对照，锚点保持一致；五维评分与 FY2023 完全相同，因为折旧政策、年限假设、减值记录、CAPEX 强度与行业暴露均未发生真实变化，差异仅体现为 Xilinx 并表首年的事实性细节（收购分摊金额、当期摊销费用、两次商誉测试）。

company.name: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.
company.industry: Semiconductors / Fabless Chip Design (CPU, GPU, DPU, FPGA, Adaptive SoC)
company.primary_assets: Acquisition-related Intangibles and Goodwill (Xilinx acquired 2022-02-14, Pensando acquired 2022-05-26 - both first consolidated in FY2022), small fabless PP&E base, technology licenses
company.coverage_note: AMD财年为12月最后一个周六截止的52/53周年度，FY2022止2022-12-31，签署日期2023-02-27（HTML L5045）。FY2022是Xilinx（2022-02-14完成，对价$48.8B）与Pensando（2022-05-26完成，对价$1.9B）并表首年：收购形成商誉$22,784M+$1,098M、可辨认无形资产$27,308M+$349M，当期确认收购无形资产摊销$3,548M。

financial_highlights.amortization_note: Amortization is entirely acquisition-related intangibles (Xilinx/Pensando): income statement split $1,448M in cost of sales + $2,100M in operating expenses (HTML L3203); Note 6 states 'Acquisition-related intangible amortization expense was $3.5 billion in fiscal year 2022' (L3814); cash flow statement combined 'Depreciation and amortization' was $4,174M in FY2022 (vs $407M FY2021)
financial_highlights.impairment_note: No goodwill impairment in FY2022: tested twice - Q2 2022 immediately prior to and after the segment reporting change ('no indicators of impairment', L3822-3823) and Q4 2022 annual test ('no goodwill impairment with respect to its reporting units', L3824-3826); MD&A confirms fair values of all reporting units exceeded carrying values (L2884-2886). No PP&E or intangible impairment charge identified in the filing. FY2022 Q3 did have realized inventory/pricing-related charges in Gaming and Client segments (L1675-1677), amount not separately disclosed - inventory class, not depreciable/amortizable assets.
financial_highlights.gilti_note: FY2022 GILTI tax accounting method change increased net income by $296M (L3592-3595) - a tax policy election driven by the Xilinx acquisition, NOT a depreciation/amortization estimate change; recorded here for transparency, excluded from D2 scoring

accounting_policy.leasehold_improvements: shorter of the remaining terms of the leases or the estimated useful economic lives of the improvements
accounting_policy.equipment_life_note: FY2022 10-K Note 2 discloses 'one to 15 years for equipment' (L3479-3480); FY2023 10-K discloses 'two to 15 years' - lower-bound wording differs by one year, upper bound 15 years identical; no disclosure of a change, treated as same schedule for anchoring
accounting_policy.intangible_amortization_method: over the assets' estimated useful lives based on the pattern in which the economic benefits are expected to be received to cost of sales and operating expenses
accounting_policy.iprd_policy: IPR&D (Xilinx $970M + Pensando $220M) recorded as indefinite-lived intangible, not amortized until technological feasibility; tested for impairment annually and upon indicators (L3770-3779)
accounting_policy.goodwill_impairment_testing: Annual test as of the first day of Q4 at reporting-unit level (Data Center, Gaming, Embedded after Q2 2022 segment change), qualitative-first with quantitative option; FY2022 tested twice (Q2 segment reassignment + Q4 annual), both concluded no impairment
accounting_policy.longlived_asset_impairment_testing: Reviewed if indicators exist (indicators reviewed quarterly); grouped at lowest level of identifiable cash flows; undiscounted cash flow recoverability test, write-down to fair value if not recoverable (L3384-3404)
accounting_policy.change_in_estimate_method: NA - no change in depreciation/amortization estimate disclosed in FY2022; the word 'prospectively' does not appear in this filing (0 hits), unlike Meta's 10-K. FY2022 does contain two tax-related accounting changes (GILTI method change +$296M net income, L3577-3597; tax interest reclassification $11M, L3599-3620), neither related to depreciation/amortization lives
accounting_policy.policy_risk_note: AMD is fabless: PP&E is only $1,513M net (2.2% of total assets), so direct depreciation risk is small. The economically dominant lifetime assumptions were set at initial recognition in FY2022: Xilinx developed technology $12,295M over 16 years and customer relationships $12,290M over 14 years (L3753) - assigned in the same year the company itself discloses 1-2 year product iteration pressure ('rapid technological changes, frequent product introductions', L1165-1167; 'short product lifecycles...rapid obsolescence', L1657-1659). No useful-life extension history and no 'prospectively' change language found, but the initial assignment of 14-16 year lives to newly acquired adaptive-computing technology embeds the optimistic-lifetime bias in amortization rather than depreciation - identical pattern to FY2023 confirmed version.

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Note 2. Basis of Presentation and Significant Accounting Policies
risk_signals.keyword_matched: estimated useful lives of one to 15 years for equipment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Property and equipment are stated at cost. Depreciation and amortization are provided on a straight-line basis over the estimated useful lives of one to 15 years for equipment, 34 to 44 years for buildings, and leasehold improvements are measured by the shorter of the remaining terms of the leases or the estimated useful economic lives of the improvements.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 2. Basis of Presentation and Significant Accounting Policies - Property and Equipment (HTML lines 3477-3482)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Official depreciation assumption: straight-line, equipment 1-15 years. The 15-year upper bound is extremely long for a company whose own risk factors describe short product lifecycles and rapid obsolescence. Implied average equipment life from the statements (depreciation $439M vs equipment gross $2,163M) is roughly 5 years. However, PP&E net is only $1,513M (2.2% of total assets), so the direct profit leverage of this assumption is small for a fabless designer. Anchor note: identical policy to FY2023 confirmed version (which disclosed 'two to 15 years'; upper bound unchanged at 15).
evidence_chain: Stated equipment depreciation life: 1-15 years, straight-line
Implied average equipment life approx. 5 years (depreciation $439M / equipment gross $2,163M)
AMD's own risk factors describe short product lifecycles with rapid obsolescence (see SIG-002)
Upper-bound 15-year life assumes zero technological displacement for a decade and a half
Mitigating fact: fabless model means PP&E is tiny ($1.5B net), so even aggressive lives move profit by little
Result: direction of bias is under-depreciation, but magnitude is limited by the small asset base

risk_signals.keyword_matched: short product lifecycles, which can lead to rapid obsolescence
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Many of our markets are characterized by short product lifecycles, which can lead to rapid obsolescence and price erosion.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: AMD's own admission that its product markets have short lifecycles and rapid obsolescence directly contradicts multi-year depreciation/amortization assumptions for the assets that embody the same technology (equipment up to 15 years; acquired Xilinx developed technology 16 years, customer relationships 14 years - both newly booked in FY2022). The economic value of the technology evaporates faster than the balance sheet releases it.
evidence_chain: Company states: short product lifecycles, rapid obsolescence, price erosion
Semiconductor/AI product generation cycle in the industry is approximately 1-2 years
Depreciation/amortization schedules assume the same technology generates economic benefit for 5-16 years
Contradiction: revenue life of the technology (1-2 years) is far shorter than its balance-sheet life
Result: periodic depreciation/amortization expense is systematically lower than true economic consumption of the asset

risk_signals.keyword_matched: in the third quarter of 2022, we recorded certain charges
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Excess or obsolete inventory have and may in the future result in write-downs of the value of our inventory. For example, in the third quarter of 2022, we recorded certain charges primarily for inventory, pricing and related reserves in the Gaming and Client segments. Other factors that may result in excess or obsolete inventory include ... a higher incidence of inventory obsolescence because of rapidly changing technology and customer requirements.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Cross-year anchor note: in the FY2023 confirmed version this event was history; in FY2022 it is a CURRENT-YEAR realized charge. Proves the obsolescence risk is not theoretical: AMD took real charges in FY2022 Q3 when Client/Gaming products aged faster than expected amid the PC downturn (Client segment revenue -10%, unit shipments -24%, L2959-2964). Inventory is written down when obsolete, but the same technological force acts on depreciable equipment and amortizable developed technology, where no equivalent automatic write-down mechanism exists unless a formal impairment trigger is declared.
evidence_chain: FY2022 Q3 (current year): actual charges for inventory, pricing and related reserves in Gaming and Client
Cause admitted by company: rapidly changing technology and customer requirements
Inventory gets marked down quickly; fixed assets and intangibles carrying the same technology risk do not
Depreciation schedules assume smooth consumption; reality is step-function obsolescence events
Result: obsolescence losses show up late and lumpy (impairment) instead of early and smooth (higher depreciation), flattering interim profits

risk_signals.keyword_matched: we recorded significant goodwill and other intangible assets on our consolidated balance sheet
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Any impairment of our tangible, definite-lived intangible or indefinite-lived intangible assets, including goodwill, may adversely impact our financial position and results of operations. ... In connection with the Xilinx and Pensando acquisitions, we recorded significant goodwill and other intangible assets on our consolidated balance sheet. ... A decrease in the long-term economic outlook and future cash flows of our business could significantly impact asset values and potentially result in the impairment of goodwill and may require us to record future goodwill impairment charges, which may have a material adverse impact on our financial position and results of operations.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: This is AMD's analog of Meta's data-center impairment signal, freshly created in FY2022: $24.2B goodwill plus $24.1B net acquisition intangibles (71.5% of total assets) rest on 14-16 year cash-flow assumptions for acquired FPGA/adaptive-computing technology booked only months earlier (Feb/May 2022). If AI-era iteration makes Xilinx technology obsolete faster than the amortization schedule assumes, the shortfall surfaces as a large one-time impairment - i.e., catch-up amortization that should have been recognized earlier.
evidence_chain: Xilinx ($48.8B, Feb 2022) and Pensando ($1.9B, May 2022) acquisitions created $24.2B goodwill + $27.7B gross intangibles in FY2022
Amortization assumes 14-16 year lives for developed technology and customer relationships
Company itself warns impairment indicators include inability to introduce new products or achieve forecasts (L2261-2264)
AI accelerator iteration (1-2 years) can strand acquired product roadmaps
If triggered, impairment = belated recognition of under-amortization in prior periods
Result: prior-period profits inflated relative to a faster amortization schedule; tail risk of a large one-time charge, concentrated in Embedded reporting unit ($21,055M goodwill)

risk_signals.keyword_matched: changes in competing technologies, and changes to the business strategy may represent an indicator of impairment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: We may incur future impairments of our technology license purchases. We license certain third-party technologies and tools for the design and production of our products. ... Factors such as the life of the assets, changes in competing technologies, and changes to the business strategy may represent an indicator of impairment. The occurrence of any of these events may require us to record future technology license impairment charges.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Direct acknowledgment that 'changes in competing technologies' can impair capitalized technology assets (software and technology licenses, net $362M, L3628). The same logic applies to all technology-carrying assets on the balance sheet: the carrying amounts assume continued relevance that competing technology can destroy at any time.
evidence_chain: Capitalized technology licenses carried as other non-current assets ($362M net)
Impairment indicators include changes in competing technologies
Competing-technology change in AI silicon currently occurs on a 1-2 year cadence
Amortization of these licenses assumes stable utility over their asset life
Result: another channel by which technology transition forces belated catch-up charges

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Note 5 (Business Combinations) / Note 6 (Acquisition-related Intangible Assets and Goodwill)
risk_signals.keyword_matched: Developed technology $12,295 16 years / weighted-average estimated useful life
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Following are details of the purchase consideration allocated to acquired intangible assets: Developed technology $12,295 million, weighted-average estimated useful life 16 years; Customer relationships $12,290 million, 14 years; Customer backlog $793 million, 1 year; Corporate trade name $65 million, 1 year; Product trademarks $895 million, 12 years; Identified intangible assets subject to amortization $26,338 million; IPR&D not subject to amortization $970 million; Total identified intangible assets acquired $27,308 million (Xilinx allocation table). Acquisition-related intangible amortization expense was $3.5 billion in fiscal year 2022.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 5. Business Combinations - Xilinx intangible allocation (HTML line 3753); Xilinx goodwill $22,784M and purchase consideration $48,793M (line 3744); Note 6 intangibles table and amortization expense (line 3814)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: The strongest quantitative evidence in AMD's FY2022 filing, and the origin year of the exposure: AMD assumes Xilinx adaptive-computing technology acquired in February 2022 will generate economic benefit until ~2038 (16 years) and its customer relationships until ~2036 (14 years). An additional $970M of Xilinx IPR&D sits as indefinite-lived and will begin amortization only upon technological feasibility (the FY2023 10-K later showed it reclassified at 15 years). This is the same optimistic-lifetime pattern as Meta's 4-5 year servers, but far more extreme in duration, sitting in amortization rather than depreciation.
evidence_chain: Xilinx developed technology: $12.3B amortized over 16 years; customer relationships: $12.3B over 14 years (assigned at acquisition, Feb 2022)
$970M Xilinx IPR&D + $220M Pensando IPR&D held as indefinite-lived, amortization deferred until feasibility
FY2022 acquisition-intangible amortization expense: $3,548M (vs net income of only $1,320M)
If true economic life of the technology is 5-7 years rather than 14-16, annual amortization is understated by a factor of 2-3x on these assets
Result: amortization expense materially understated relative to technology reality; reported margins and EPS flattered from the first consolidation year

risk_signals.source: Consolidated Statements of Operations; MD&A - All Other Category / Results of Operations
risk_signals.text_excerpt: All Other operating loss of $5.0 billion in 2022 primarily consisted of $3.5 billion of amortization of acquisition-related intangibles, $1.1 billion of stock-based compensation expense, and $452 million of acquisition-related costs ... The decrease in gross margin was primarily due to amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition. ... The decrease in operating income was primarily driven by amortization of intangible assets associated with the Xilinx acquisition.
risk_signals.page_location: MD&A (HTML lines 2990-2996, 2623-2628); Consolidated Statements of Operations: amortization $1,448M in cost of sales + $2,100M in operating expenses (line 3203); segment table All Other amortization $3,548M (line 3661)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Quantifies the profit leverage of the lifetime assumptions in the first consolidation year: $3,548M amortization = 15.0% of revenue and 2.7x FY2022 net income of $1,320M. Operating income fell to $1,264M from $3,648M primarily because of this amortization; gross margin fell 48% -> 45% primarily due to Xilinx intangible amortization. Had the acquired technology been assigned lives closer to the 1-2 year cycle the risk factors describe, FY2022 would have been near breakeven at the operating line - the 14-16 year assumption is what keeps the acquisition accretive on paper.
evidence_chain: FY2022 amortization of acquisition-related intangibles: $3,548M (COGS $1,448M + opex $2,100M)
Equals 2.7x net income ($1,320M) and 15.0% of revenue
Management attributes both the gross-margin decline and the operating-income decline primarily to this amortization
All Other operating loss of $4,979M is dominated by the $3,548M amortization
Result: the income statement already shows the amortization burden; any acceleration toward economic reality would erase most reported profit

risk_signals.source: MD&A - Critical Accounting Estimates / Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm (Critical Audit Matter)
risk_signals.text_excerpt: Significant estimates in valuing developed technology, in-process research and development, customer relationships and other identifiable intangible assets include, but are not limited to, expected future revenue growth rates and margins, future changes in technology, time to recreate customer relationships, useful lives, and discount rates. ... (Auditor CAM - Business Combination): The significant assumptions used to estimate the value of these intangible assets included certain assumptions that form the basis of the forecasted results, specifically, revenue growth rates, technology migration curves, and time to recreate customer relationships. These significant assumptions are forward looking and could be affected by future economic and market conditions.
risk_signals.page_location: MD&A Critical Accounting Estimates - Business Combinations (HTML lines 2810-2822); Report of Independent Registered Public Accounting Firm, Critical Audit Matters (lines 4466-4484)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Both management and the auditor flag technology change as a key assumption in the Xilinx valuation, and E&Y elevated the Xilinx business combination to a Critical Audit Matter - meaning estimate error in the developed-technology/customer-relationship fair values (and hence their 16/14-year amortization bases) is among the most consequential judgments in the FY2022 audit. 'Technology migration curves' is effectively an admission that the acquired technology is expected to migrate/be replaced - yet the amortization schedule still spreads it over 14-16 years.
evidence_chain: Management: intangible fair values depend on 'future changes in technology' and 'useful lives'
E&Y CAM: Xilinx acquisition accounting involved significant estimation uncertainty; assumptions include 'technology migration curves'
The same forward-looking technology assumptions underpin the amortization lives, where estimation error reverses only through impairment
FY2022 Q3 inventory charges (SIG-003) already demonstrated estimate fragility around technology pace in the same fiscal year
Result: documented estimate fragility around technology pace; supports downgrading confidence in long amortization lives

risk_signals.source: Item 1A. Risk Factors - Acquisitions and Joint Ventures
risk_signals.keyword_matched: amortization expenses and write-downs of acquired assets
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In addition, to complete an acquisition, we may issue equity securities, which would dilute our stockholders' ownership and could adversely affect the price of our common stock, and/or incur debt, assume contingent liabilities or have amortization expenses and write-downs of acquired assets, which could adversely affect our results of operations.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Explicit warning that acquisitions bring both amortization expenses AND write-downs of acquired assets - management pairs the two as the expected cost pattern of deals like Xilinx/Pensando. This acknowledges ex ante that the amortization schedule may not fully capture the economic consumption of acquired assets and that write-downs (impairments) are a foreseeable complement.
evidence_chain: Company discloses acquisitions entail 'amortization expenses and write-downs of acquired assets'
FY2022 closed two acquisitions totaling ~$50.7B of consideration
Amortization ($3,548M) materialized immediately in FY2022; write-downs remain the deferred half of the pair
Result: management's own framing supports treating amortization understatement and future impairment as linked risks

risk_signals.keyword_matched: competition will continue to be intense due to rapid technological changes
risk_signals.text_excerpt: We expect that competition will continue to be intense due to rapid technological changes, frequent product introductions by our competitors or new competitors of products that may provide better performance/experience or that may include additional features that render our products comparatively less competitive.
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Management's own characterization of its competitive environment: rapid technological changes with frequent competitor product introductions. This is the forcing function that shortens the economic life of everything technology-linked on AMD's balance sheet - equipment, technology licenses, and especially the $27.3B of Xilinx intangibles booked this year over 14-16 year horizons.
evidence_chain: Competition expected to remain intense due to 'rapid technological changes, frequent product introductions'
Direct competitors named in the filing: Intel (heavier R&D/manufacturing resources, L958-963) and NVIDIA (graphics/GPU, L971)
Technology substitution pressure applies to acquired Xilinx FPGA/adaptive technology as much as to AMD's own products
14-16 year amortization lives assume recoverability the Risk Factors contradict
Result: accounting life exceeds competitively-defensible economic life of acquired technology assets

risk_signals.source: Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements - Note 6; MD&A Critical Accounting Estimates - Goodwill
risk_signals.keyword_matched: concluded that there was no goodwill impairment
risk_signals.text_excerpt: In the second quarter of fiscal year 2022, the Company reassigned goodwill balances among the updated reportable segments to reflect changes in its segment reporting structure. The Company performed a goodwill impairment test immediately prior to and after the segment change and determined that no indicators of impairment to goodwill existed. ... During the fourth quarter of fiscal years 2022 and 2021, the Company conducted its annual impairment tests of goodwill and concluded that there was no goodwill impairment with respect to its reporting units. ... Based on our annual impairment testing, the fair values of all of our reporting units exceeded their carrying values.
risk_signals.page_location: Note 6. Acquisition-related Intangible Assets and Goodwill (HTML lines 3819-3826); MD&A Critical Accounting Estimates - Goodwill (lines 2884-2886)
risk_signals.relevance_to_depreciation: Negative/absence signal: unlike Meta (which took a $2.43B facilities impairment in FY2023), AMD recorded zero impairment on depreciable/amortizable assets in FY2022 and passed goodwill tests twice (Q2 segment reassignment and Q4 annual). This lowers the realized-trigger score (D3) for AMD, but note the goodwill was on the books for less than eleven months and tested largely qualitatively - the cushion on $24.2B of freshly-created goodwill was never stress-tested by a full technology cycle.
evidence_chain: FY2022 impairment charges on PP&E/intangibles/goodwill: $0
Goodwill tested twice in FY2022 (Q2 segment change + Q4 annual); both concluded no impairment
Embedded reporting unit carries $21,055M of the $24,177M goodwill (87%)
Absence of impairment is not evidence of absence of overvaluation - goodwill was <1 year old and Q4 test was qualitative-first
Result: no realized trigger this year; impairment remains a latent tail risk concentrated in the Embedded/Xilinx reporting unit

dimension_scores.dimension_name: 折旧年限 vs 技术实际寿命
dimension_scores.dimension_name_en: Depreciation Life vs Technology Useful Life
dimension_scores.reasoning: 与FY2023确认版锚点一致（3分）：设备折旧年限披露为1-15年直线法（Note 2，L3477-3482；FY2023版为'2-15年'，仅下限措辞差一年、上限15年一致，无变更披露），按折旧费用$439M/设备原值$2,163M推算隐含平均设备年限约5年，处于4-6年锚点区间；但AMD是fabless设计公司，PP&E净额仅$1,513M（占总资产2.2%），1-2年迭代压力首先冲击其产品和收购来的技术资产而非自有设备。真正极端的年限错配在收购无形资产：FY2022并表首年即给Xilinx开发技术定16年、客户关系定14年（$12,295M/$12,290M，L3753），另有$970M Xilinx IPR&D+$220M Pensando IPR&D作为无限期资产挂账待摊，而公司自己在Risk Factors承认'short product lifecycles...rapid obsolescence'（L1657-1659）与'rapid technological changes'（L1165-1167）。综合：直接折旧错配有限、摊销错配极端，取中档3分。

与FY2023确认版锚点一致（2分）：全文检索'prospectively'零命中——FY2022没有任何折旧/摊销年限变更披露，既无延长年限+未来适用（Meta式5分情形），也无历史延长记录，属于'无变更→2-3'的相对保守情形，给2分。需透明披露的两项FY2022会计变更均为税务类、与折旧/摊销无关：GILTI税会计方法变更（+$296M净利润，L3577-3597）与税利息重分类（$11M，L3599-3620）。另注：公司在收购初始计量时给Xilinx开发技术定16年、客户关系14年的超长年限，等于把乐观假设前置到初始确认而非后续变更；该激进性已计入D1/D3，不在D2重复扣分（与FY2023版处理口径一致）。

与FY2023确认版锚点一致（3分）：FY2022可折旧/可摊销资产实际减值为零——商誉在Q2（分部变更前后）与Q4（年度）两次测试均通过（L3819-3826），MD&A确认所有报告单元公允价值超过账面值（L2884-2886），无Meta式已实现大额减值。直接减值信号数量不少但均指向商誉/无形资产/技术许可/存货而非自有PP&E：①Risk Factors专章警告Xilinx/Pensando形成的商誉及有形/无形资产可能减值（L2237-2269）；②技术许可减值风险专章（L2447-2456）；③存货过时减记风险且FY2022 Q3已在Gaming/Client实际发生（本期实现，L1673-1683）——但属存货类而非可折旧资产；④收购风险明示'amortization expenses and write-downs of acquired assets'（L2205-2210）；⑤Note 2长期资产减值政策（L3384-3404）。对'折旧'狭义口径而言属于间接信号，按'仅间接→3'锚点给3分；商誉+无形资产合计$48,295M占总资产71.5%，Embedded报告单元单扛$21,055M商誉（87%），尾部风险集中且为并表首年、未经完整技术周期检验。

与FY2023确认版锚点一致（1分）：FY2022 CAPEX（购置不动产与设备）$450M，CAPEX/收入=1.91%，低于3%锚点下限，典型fabless轻资产结构（对比Meta 20.2%；FY2023版为2.41%同档）。折旧费用$439M仅占收入1.9%，即使折旧年限假设严重失真，对利润的杠杆效应也小。真正的利润杠杆在收购无形资产摊销（$3,548M，占收入15.0%，为净利润的2.7倍），但该口径不属于CAPEX强度维度，已在D1/D3反映。按'<5%→1-2'锚点给1分。

与FY2023确认版锚点一致（3分）：AMD直接处于AI/高性能芯片竞争中心（Data Center部门收入$6,043M、+64%），公司在Risk Factors中明言竞争将因'rapid technological changes, frequent product introductions'持续激烈（L1164-1169），并承认市场'short product lifecycles...rapid obsolescence'（L1657-1659），竞争对手点名Intel与NVIDIA。但按维度口径，AMD是卖芯片而非运营GPU资产的一方：技术替代风险通过存货减记（FY2022 Q3已实际发生）、无形资产/商誉减值、定价压力传导，而非通过自有算力资产折旧。属于'卖芯片而非运营、间接暴露→2-3'区间，考虑到其对NVIDIA/Intel迭代节奏的直接跟随压力及Xilinx收购技术资产的高暴露（并表首年$27.3B），取区间上限3分。

composite_score.confidence_reason: All key figures verified against filing text (revenue, net income, CAPEX, depreciation, amortization, PP&E, goodwill, intangibles, useful lives, Xilinx/Pensando allocation tables). Direct depreciation-specific signals are inherently limited for a fabless company; scoring relies partly on the amortization schedule of acquired intangibles as the analogous optimistic-lifetime exposure - the same judgment call as the FY2023 confirmed version, with which all five dimension scores are anchored identically.

cross_year_anchor_comparison.conclusion: 五维评分与综合分同FY2023确认版完全一致，符合锚点一致军规：两版之间折旧政策（直线法、设备上限15年）、年限变更记录（均无、'prospectively'均0命中）、已实现减值（均为$0）、CAPEX强度（1.91% vs 2.41%，同<3%档）、行业暴露（卖芯片而非运营）均无真实政策/风险变化。分数不随年份漂移，差异仅为事实性细节。
factual_differences_fy2022_vs_fy2023: FY2022是Xilinx（2022-02-14）与Pensando（2022-05-26）并表首年：商誉$24,177M与收购无形资产$27,666M（原值）当年新入账；FY2023版对应为摊销一年后净值（商誉$24,262M含小额后续调整、无形资产净值$21,363M）
设备年限披露措辞：FY2022为'one to 15 years'（L3479-3480），FY2023为'two to 15 years'——下限差一年、上限15年一致，无变更披露，视为同一折旧表锚定
FY2022 Q3 Gaming/Client存货及定价相关费用为'本期实现'事件；FY2023版同一事件为历史记录——D3口径均归为存货类间接信号，不影响分值
FY2022商誉测试两次（Q2分部变更+Q4年度）均通过；FY2023为一次年度定性测试通过——均为零减值
FY2022新增E&Y关键审计事项'Business Combination'，明示Xilinx估值假设含'technology migration curves'；FY2023版CAM为存货估值——审计关注点在并表首年即落在收购无形资产估值上，佐证D1/D3的摊销错配主线
FY2022摊销费用$3,548M（净利润的2.7倍）为摊销暴露首个完整年份；FY2023版为$2,811M（净利润的3.3倍），金额下降系客户积压/商号等短年限资产摊完所致

annotation_methodology.source_document: Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. FY2022 Annual Report on Form 10-K (fiscal year ended December 31, 2022, signed February 27, 2023)
annotation_methodology.filing_accessed: Local file: data/raw/amd_fy2022_10k.html (5,049 lines, originally from SEC EDGAR, CIK 0000002488)
annotation_methodology.text_extraction_method: Case-insensitive keyword search (impairment, useful life/lives, depreciation, amortization, obsolescence, prospectively, straight-line, technology migration) on tag-stripped per-line text with HTML line-number preservation; every candidate hit manually verified in visible body text; hidden XBRL tag matches excluded. Financial figures extracted from Consolidated Statements of Operations, Balance Sheets, Cash Flows (all embedded in HTML line 3203), Note 2, Note 5, Note 6 and MD&A.
annotation_methodology.scoring_method: Five-dimension weighted scoring (D1 0.25 / D2 0.20 / D3 0.20 / D4 0.20 / D5 0.15), 1-5 integer scale per dimension, weighted average mapped to risk levels (>=4 High #DC3545; 3-3.9 Medium-High #FD7E14; 2-2.9 Medium #FFC107; <2 Low #28A745). Cross-year anchoring: all five dimension scores held identical to the AMD FY2023 confirmed version because no real policy/risk change occurred between the two filings.
annotation_methodology.human_verification: Pending review by project lead; all text excerpts quoted verbatim from the filing with line numbers
annotation_methodology.limitation: Single-year 10-K; AMD discloses equipment useful life only as a 1-15 year range with no per-class breakdown, so the implied average equipment life (~5 years) is an analyst estimate. FY2022 Q3 inventory/pricing charge amount is not separately quantified in this filing (marked 0/NA for asset impairment). Depreciation-specific signals are structurally sparse for a fabless issuer; amortization of acquisition intangibles was used as the analogous exposure, the same methodological judgment as the FY2023 confirmed version. Pensando purchase price allocation was still preliminary at FY2022 year-end (measurement period open up to one year).
